title: Getting Data You Can Trust
audience: Basic science researchers new to AI
objectives: Audit a consent protocol for comprehension rather than signature.
Cost out the strategies needed to close a representation gap.
Judge whether a security protocol protects against re-identification.
Quantify inter-annotator agreement and decide how many annotators are needed.
Map source records to the OMOP common data model using concept IDs.

sections.name: Audit selector
sections.purpose: Five audits behind one segmented control at the top of the page.
sections.how_to_use: Click a chip to switch audit. Only the selected audit renders, and the choice is held in session state, so a widget that triggers a rerun does not lose your place. Work all five.

sections.name: Audit 1 - Consent (Autonomy)
sections.purpose: Judge whether a consent form was actually understood.
sections.how_to_use: Move the language-complexity select_slider through its three steps. 'Technical jargon' leaves the legal text alone; 'Standard' and 'Simplified' each show their own revised wording beside it, so every move changes what is on screen. Only 'Simplified' is rated compliant.

sections.name: Audit 2 - Representation (Justice)
sections.purpose: Cost out what closing a representation gap actually takes.
sections.how_to_use: Name the missing group, set the target-proportion slider, then tick the three strategy checkboxes (community liaisons +10%, translated materials +5%, logistical support +10%). The bar chart and pass/fail verdict update. The baseline is a fixed 5% for passive recruitment.

sections.name: Audit 3 - Security (Privacy)
sections.purpose: Recognise that de-identification alone is not protection.
sections.how_to_use: Tick the four security layers. All four gives SECURE; two or three gives VULNERABLE; fewer gives CRITICAL RISK. The activity opens at CRITICAL RISK by design, because nothing is checked yet.

sections.name: Audit 4 - Label Quality
sections.purpose: Establish that a model cannot be more reliable than its labels.
sections.how_to_use: Simulated researchers annotate variants as pathogenic or benign. Set the number of variants, researchers, and the disagreement rate, then read the ICC metric, the high-disagreement table (candidates for re-review), and the accuracy-vs-number-of-annotators curve, whose elbow answers 'how many annotators can we afford'.

sections.name: Audit 5 - Common Vocabulary
sections.purpose: Make the data readable outside your own lab.
sections.how_to_use: Set the donor count and seed, then follow the three steps: raw donor-registry records, the OMOP person table (names and addresses removed, demographics replaced by concept IDs such as 8507 for male), and condition_occurrence mapped from ICD-10.

chatbot_guidance: The audit target is ImmPort; the subject is a donor and the sample is a biological specimen.

At the default 20% disagreement rate the ICC is negative. That is not a bug: it means the researchers disagree with each other more than the variants differ, so the label carries no signal. The page explains this.
Genomic data cannot be truly de-identified, because the sequence is the identifier. That is why the security tab matters more here than it looks.
The OMOP demo runs on both tracks; it is what has to happen before specimen metadata can be pooled with another site's.
Every chart on this page has a 'View chart data as text (accessible alternative)' expander beneath it, holding the same numbers as a table.
